content.title: About
content.content: Yogurt with almond milk is a blended beverage that mixes traditional dairy yogurt with plant‑based almond milk. It has a smooth, creamy taste with a subtle nutty note and a velvety texture. Suitable as a stand‑alone snack or as a base for smoothies, desserts, and breakfasts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The combination delivers a double dose of probiotics from the yogurt and plant nutrients from the almond milk.
Almond milk is lower in calories and fat than cow’s milk while retaining a pleasant nutty aroma.
Yogurt‑almond milk drinks are often fortified with vitamin D and calcium to support bone health.
The product is popular among vegetarians and those with lactose intolerance because part of the dairy is replaced with a plant component.
In some countries it is served frozen as a “yogurt ice‑cream cocktail.”

items.title: Probiotics
items.content: Yogurt provides live bacterial cultures that support gut health and the immune system.

items.title: Protein
items.content: The blend offers a good source of complete protein, essential for muscle and tissue maintenance.

items.title: Vitamin E
items.content: Almond milk is rich in vitamin E, a powerful antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Calcium
items.content: Yogurt is a calcium source, and almond milk is often fortified, together promoting strong bones.

items.title: Reduced lactose
items.content: Lowering the proportion of dairy reduces lactose content, making it more suitable for people with mild lactose intolerance.

items.title: Milk allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to cow’s milk may still react to the yogurt component, even with almond milk added.

items.title: Tree‑nut allergy
items.content: Almond milk contains nut proteins that can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Flavored versions may contain added sugars; choose unsweetened options if blood‑glucose control is a concern.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: While almond milk is low‑calorie, the yogurt base adds calories; portion control is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink it straight, blend into smoothies, pour over granola, stir into oatmeal, create parfaits, or freeze for a creamy ice‑cream alternative.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 1‑4 °C. After opening, consume within 5‑7 days. Do not freeze, as the texture may separate.
